newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Six Shi'ite Moslems to stand trial on Saturday.
newsitem.headline: Six Shi'ite Moslems to stand trial on Saturday.

text.p: Six Bahraini Shi'ite Moslems will go on trial on Saturday on charges of possessing unlawful leaflets, a lawyer said on Thursday.
"The group will stand trial on Saturday," the lawyer, who asked not to be named, told Reuters.
The six, arrested in April 1996, are Hassan Qassab, Shaker al-Mahouzi, Mirza al-Qatari, Saleh Hassan, Ali Isa Ahmed and Hussain Howaida, he said.
"They were accused of possessing leaflets containing false news and statements without any reason," the lawyer said, adding "I expect a maximum penalty of two years in jail."
In March, Bahrain jailed 36 Shi'ites for being involved in a pro-Iranian plot to topple the government by force.
Shi'ite Moslems have waged sporadic protests, bombing and arson attacks since December 1994 to demand political and economic reforms by the Sunni-led government.

A series of fires hit the island state, the Gulf's financial and banking centre, this week causing damage but there were no reports of casualties. A government official said on Thursday some of the fires were premeditated.
Two fires destroyed three Asian-owned shops in the capital late on Wednesday, witnesses said, adding that two cars parked nearby were damaged.

"A premeditated fire, which broke out in the early hours of Thursday, destroyed a cold store and a flat above it. Two cars parked nearby had also been damaged," the official told Reuters. There were no casualties, he said.
Earlier on Wednesday, another fire destroyed a flat in a Manama district, causing damage but no casualties.

On Tuesday, fire destroyed a shop in the Shi'ite village of Khamis and the official said the blaze was also premeditated. on Monday firefighters were seen battling blazes in Sanabis village and nearby areas.

Riots said by witnesses to have been sparked by the death of a man arrested during earlier protests broke out in Sanabis on Monday. Bahrain's official Gulf News Agency said security forces broke up the disturbance and arrested a number of riot leaders.
